title: LegacyWorld: Atomicity-Aware Evaluation of GUI Agents for Legacy Workflows
abstract: arXiv:2608.14131v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Legacy and legacy-like enterprise systems often remain difficult to modernize because critical workflows expose limited programmable interfaces and still require manual GUI interaction. This paper reports a pre-deployment evaluation study motivated by the development of legacy-use, an industry-oriented framework for automating such workflows with multimodal LLM agents. During framework development, domain experts helped identify stateful workflows where successful demos are not sufficient: a failed agent run may still leave persistent invalid changes in business or healthcare records. We therefore evaluate computer-use agents using atomicity: a run should either complete the intended workflow correctly or fail without unintended persistent side effects. translated_title: 遗产世界：面向遗产工作流的GUI代理的原子性感知评估
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2608.14131v1 公告类型：新 摘要：遗产和类似遗产的企业系统通常难以现代化，因为关键工作流暴露了有限的可编程接口，仍需手动GUI交互。本文报告了一项部署前评估研究，该研究受“legacy-use”框架开发启发，这是一个面向行业的多模态LLM代理自动化此类工作流的框架。在框架开发过程中，领域专家帮助识别了有状态工作流，其中成功的演示并不足够：失败的代理运行可能仍会在业务或医疗记录中留下持久的无效更改。因此，我们使用原子性来评估计算机使用代理：一次运行应要么正确完成预期工作流，要么失败且不产生意外的持久副作用。我们构建了一个由领域专家知情的基准，包含28个Windows GUI工作流，每个工作流指定了初始状态、目标状态和特定任务的验证器。我们比较了专家编写的提示词...
tldr: 本文提出并评估了基于原子性标准的GUI代理，确保在遗产工作流中，代理运行要么成功完成要么无副作用失败，并构建了28个Windows GUI工作流的专家基准。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes and evaluates GUI agents based on atomicity criteria, ensuring that in legacy workflows, agent runs either succeed or fail without side effects, and constructs an expert-informed benchmark of 28 Windows GUI workflows.
